title: Transfer of Property Act, 1882
snippet: A lease creates a right to enjoy immovable property for a term in consideration of price paid; lessor and lessee rights and liabilities are governed by the lease deed and the Act.

title: Transfer of Property Act, 1882
snippet: In the absence of contract or local usage, leases for agriculture or non-agriculture purposes terminate only by notice of specified duration; wrongful termination may be challenged in civil court.

title: Transfer of Property Act, 1882
snippet: The lessor must give quiet enjoyment; the lessee must pay rent, maintain the property, and not commit waste; breach can lead to forfeiture or suit for possession and arrears.

title: Registration Act, 1908
snippet: Documents such as leases above certain terms and sale deeds generally require registration; unregistered documents may not confer enforceable rights in many situations.

title: Indian Contract Act, 1872
snippet: Rent agreements are contracts; breach, forfeiture clauses, and deposit disputes are decided on contract terms read with rent-control and transfer laws.

title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
snippet: Promoters must register projects, disclose sanctioned plans, and adhere to timelines; allottees may seek refund, interest, or compensation for delay or misrepresentation before the Authority or Adjudicating Officer.

title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
snippet: Willful failure to comply with RERA orders or fraudulent practices attracts penalties and imprisonment as specified; complaints can be filed with the Regulatory Authority.

title: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (State adoption)
snippet: Where States adopt model provisions, security deposit caps, rent revision rules, and eviction grounds are codified; actual rights depend on the State tenancy law in force.

title: State Rent Control / Tenancy statutes
snippet: Many States have Rent Acts protecting tenants from arbitrary eviction and regulating deposit and increase; eviction usually requires notice and often only on specified grounds before a court or rent tribunal.

title: Specific Relief Act, 1963
snippet: Parties may seek possession or permanent and mandatory injunctions in property disputes; courts balance hardship and conduct of parties when granting relief.

title: Indian Easements Act, 1882
snippet: Rights of way and easements can arise by grant or prescription; obstruction may be remedied by injunction or declaration in civil suits.

title: Land Revenue / Mutation rules (State)
snippet: Mutation and khata entries are updated through revenue authorities; disputes on title or boundary may require civil suits or revenue tribunals depending on State law.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (housing services)
snippet: Flat buyers may file consumer complaints against builders for delay, defective construction, or unfair trade practice where jurisdiction and pecuniary limits are met.

title: Anonymized tenant defence · Pune district
section: Illustrative outcome: eviction suit resisted with registered lease
snippet: Anonymized pattern from Pune area: a tenant produced a registered lease, rent receipts, and proof of timely NEFT transfers; when the landlord rushed an eviction notice without stated grounds under the rent law, the tenant filed before the civil court and obtained status-quo during pendency. Outcomes depend on facts; illustrative note only.

title: Anonymized deposit dispute · Pune district
section: Illustrative outcome: deposit largely forfeited (weak paperwork)
snippet: Anonymized pattern from Pune district: a flatmate left after an informal WhatsApp deal, paid deposit in cash without receipt, and could not show a clear termination date; the owner deducted most of the deposit for alleged damages and the tenant recovered little in negotiation. Written terms and traceable payments matter. Not a judgment.
forum_visited: Police mediation / informal negotiation (no suit filed)

title: Anonymized RERA refund · Gurugram district
section: Illustrative outcome: allottee received refund order
snippet: Anonymized pattern from Gurugram: a buyer filed before H-RERA with builder-buyer agreement, demand letters, and delay logs; after show-cause the authority directed refund with interest for prolonged default. Another buyer who missed limitation steps faced hurdles. Illustrative pattern for learning only.
